answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. Consider a canyon as the anchor of the cost.
